subject: English

source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — English Language Grade 6
source.notes: Read directly via the Read tool (no pages param), full 128-page text extracted in one pass. Structure is unusual vs other Grade 6 subjects: 13 numbered real-world THEMES (1.0-13.0; the table of contents omits Theme 2.0 'Cultural and Religious Celebrations' and Theme 9.0 'Lifestyle Diseases' but both exist in full in the body — a source inconsistency, not a gap, resolved by reading the full body not just the TOC), each theme contributing exactly one Listening & Speaking + one Reading + one Grammar-in-Use + one Writing sub-strand (52 raw sub-strands total). The 4 official strand names per the Summary of Strands table (p.xii) are 'Listening and Speaking', 'Reading', 'Language Use', 'Writing' (labelled 'Grammar in Use' inline per-theme, 'Language Use' in the summary table and lesson-count totals — same strand, two names used inconsistently by the source itself; this file uses 'Language Use' as the canonical strand name and keeps 'Grammar in Use' as the per-theme inline label).

strandIds.ls: g6-eng-ls (13 skills: LS.1-LS.13, one per theme, kept 1:1 — each theme targets genuinely distinct phonemes/vocabulary/expressions, same precedent as Kiswahili's 19 distinct Sarufi categories staying 1:1)
strandIds.reading: g6-eng-reading (6 skills: R.1-R.6 — heavily consolidated, see rationale below)
strandIds.grammar: g6-eng-grammar (13 skills: G.1-G.13, one per theme, kept 1:1 — each theme targets a genuinely distinct grammar rule)
strandIds.writing: g6-eng-writing (11 skills: W.1-W.11 — narrative-composition sub-strands merged, see rationale below)

buildPlan.consolidationRationale: 43 skills from 52 raw sub-strands (13 themes x 4 strands). Listening&Speaking and Language Use stayed fully 1:1 (13 each) because every theme's target sounds/vocabulary (L&S) or grammar rule (Language Use) is genuinely distinct — no two themes teach the same phoneme set or the same grammar point. Reading and Writing had real, KICD-source repeats of the identical skill-type+mechanics combination across different themes (the same test this project's Kiswahili G6 precedent already established): Reading's 'Extensive Reading' sub-strand (themes 1, 5, 7, 13 — select/skim/scan/read-a-variety/library, differing only in theme flavor) merged into one R.1 skill; Reading's generic 'Intensive Reading — comprehension' sub-strand (themes 2, 3, 9, 10, 11 — predict/connect, infer vocab from context, answer direct+inferential questions, retell) merged into one R.2 skill; the three genuinely distinct Reading mechanics (4 Visuals, 6 Dialogue, 12 stress/rhythm-in-poems) and Fluency (8, speed/expression-focused, distinct from comprehension) stayed separate as R.3-R.6. Writing's 'Creative Writing — Narrative Compositions (160-200 words)' sub-strand (themes 2, 5, 8 — identical outcome text and word-count target) merged into one skill carrying scenario variety across cultural-celebrations/tourist-attractions/animal-safety framings; Writing's other Creative Writing variants (6 Pictorial, 10 Descriptive) are genuinely different composition modes and stayed separate, as did all 5 distinct Mechanics-of-Writing sub-strands (3 acronyms/abbreviations/numerals, 7 punctuation, 9 hyphen, 11 synonyms/antonyms, 13 affixes) and both distinct Functional Writing sub-strands (4 formal letter, 12 personal journal).
buildPlan.poolSizeFloor: 30+ items per fixed array (Grade 6 standard, raised from the project default 10+), 5+ distinct QuestionKinds per skill.
buildPlan.svgNote: English is vocabulary/grammar-heavy with a genuinely narrow visual angle, matching Grade 6 Kiswahili's and Grade 7/8 English's own precedent (checked: only one English skill anywhere in the project — englishG7/independentReadingVisuals.ts — uses a VisualSpec, reusing the generic bar-chart/line-graph/pie-chart types for a 'reading data visuals' sub-strand). The one Grade 6 sub-strand that explicitly names visuals (R.3, theme 4's 'Intensive Reading — Visuals') should reuse those same existing generic chart VisualSpecs rather than any new type — no new VisualSpec types needed for this subject.
